# Exact source-input transitions

The C18 input transitions are generated by `python tests/fixtures/metadata_transition/generate_task_inputs.py`.
The source-only archive binds the whole before/after documents from `3f7ec02e4` (one explicit
Shift/s.u. scalar per example) and `b9bdbf9a2` (only the declared scan Y value/free flag).
Each reversal requires the complete committed replacement; all original input and output
oracles remain intact. A saved stop rule is checked against the explicit input or the legacy
chi-square default before comparison with older saved-byte pins. No fit output supplies an
input expectation.

The release source-field projection is generated by
`python -m tests.fixtures.metadata_transition.retired_source_fields` from commit
`ec587609746b50823c048463f353b1767cbfa5f9`. It retains complete source witnesses
across exactly the removed fixed-zero second absorption coefficient and the
superseded singular stop-rule declaration (including the explicitly retained
plural chi-square-change declaration). It accepts only the complete committed
before/after bytes. Scientific values, row order, metadata, comments and extra
fields still fail closed. This projection preserves historical byte oracles;
it does not assert that different fitting policies produce identical fits.

The saved-byte adapter also validates the current plural stop-rule set against its
explicit input before removing that later field from the historical comparison.
Choices remain closed, unique and equal after scalar quoting/order is parsed;
changed, repeated, unknown or mixed declarations refuse. Every other byte and
the original full-file hashes remain checked. This is a format witness, not a
claim that different stop policies produce the same fit.


The release pin-source archive is generated by
`python -m tests.fixtures.metadata_transition.release_pin_bytes` from the same
committed release source. It retains complete before/after JSON bytes for older
source inventories, without running a fit or editing their original hashes.
Every physical reference subtree, including its tolerances, remains identical.
The sole classification exception is the named NCAF three-bank engine iteration
entry: its unchanged source description explicitly identifies a Crysta CLI
regression golden; the archived release changed reference7 to regression-pin4.
Both complete documents and this exact classification/source tuple are checked.
This is historical source compatibility, not correctness evidence for a new fit.
The later CoSiO2K input/parameter-count change is excluded from this projection.

The seed gate checks the declared stop rule against the complete archived live
source before comparing an older reconstructed tree: the earlier source predates
that declaration. Every other original seed blob remains independently pinned.


`pin_sources` fills the catalogue's missing source metadata using the last Edi
commit that contains each identical existing expected document at baseline398a48e.
It records `kind: committed-document`, the original document hash and its commit
subject. This is explicitly an archival source identity: no fit, original engine
binary or independent correctness claim is invented. Complete source documents
are archived before a surgical `source.pins` insertion. Their values, reference
classifications, tolerances and every original byte remain unchanged. The byte
adapter removes only that exact, source-bound metadata before older inventories
are checked. Simulation records expose their existing `calc.quantities` pins.
